steps.say: The crease is marking where the lifting tendon is reaching skin. Terminal fibres of the levator palpebrae superioris aponeurosis are inserting into the deep dermis and are folding the lid. Eight to ten millimetres above the lashes in women and seven to eight in men is keeping the result natural.
steps.tx: The upper eyelid crease is folded by the **levator palpebrae superioris** aponeurosis (the lid-lifting tendon) sending terminal fibres down into the deep **dermis** (the skin underside): **8** to **10** mm above the **ciliary margin** (lash line) in females, **7** to **8** mm in males. Marking respects this dimorphism; a unisex crease always looks operated.

vis.alt: Eyelid surface and cross-section showing the tarsal plate, meibomian gland, and lid layers.
vis.caption: Lid layers with the tarsal plate; the crease forms where levator fibres reach the dermis. Credit: StewardMD.

steps.say: Two fat pads and one gland are filling the upper orbit. The central preaponeurotic pad and the medial pale pad are the true fat compartments. The superolateral fullness is lacrimal gland, and resecting it is drying the eye permanently.
steps.tx: Upper eyelid fat comprises **two** compartments: the central **preaponeurotic fat pad** (in front of the levator tendon) and the **medial pale fat pad** (whiter nasal fat), with the **lacrimal gland** (the tear factory) occupying the superolateral orbital compartment. Mistaking gland for fat and resecting it causes permanent dry eye.

steps.say: Three separate fat pockets are bulging in the lower lid. Medial, central, and lateral compartments are being divided by the arcuate expansion of the inferior oblique muscle. Each pocket is herniating on its own with age, so each is being judged separately.
steps.tx: Lower eyelid fat contains **three compartments** of fat, **medial**, **central**, and **lateral** pads, separated by **arcuate expansion** (the fibrous fan) of the **inferior oblique** muscle (the eye elevator). The fan explains why one pocket bulges while its neighbour stays flat, guiding selective transposition.

**Transconjunctival** lower blepharoplasty (through the inner lid lining) enters the **retroseptal space** (the fat plane behind the septum) without violating **orbital septum** (the lid's front wall) or **orbicularis oculi** (the blink muscle), eliminating external cutaneous scarring. It suits herniated fat with tight skin; loose skin still needs a skin-excision approach.
steps.say: Fat is being reached from inside the lid with no skin cut. The transconjunctival route is entering the retroseptal space behind an intact septum and orbicularis. Younger patients with bulging fat and tight skin are suiting this scarless path.

The tear trough is being filled with living fat, not emptied. Orbital fat pedicles are being mobilised over the inferior orbital rim into a subperiosteal pocket. Hamra transposition is erasing the nasojugal groove, while simple excision is hollowing the junction.
steps.tx: **Hamra** lower eyelid fat **transposition** (vascularised pedicle slide) mobilises orbital fat pedicles over the **inferior orbital rim** (the lower eye socket edge) into the **tear trough** subperiosteal pocket (the hollow at the lid-cheek junction) to eliminate the **nasojugal groove** (the tear trough crease). Filling beats resecting: excision hollows, transposition blends.

vis.alt: Sagittal orbit sections with expanded orbital fat behind the lids and around the globe.
vis.caption: Orbital fat on sagittal section; lower blepharoplasty repositions these pads into the tear trough. Credit: StewardMD.

steps.say: Loose lids are pulling down after surgery unless they are tightened first. Distraction beyond six to eight millimetres or a slow snap-back is mandating lateral canthopexy or canthoplasty. A tight lid with a brisk snap is needing no tendon work.
steps.tx: **Snap-back test** and distraction testing (eyelid tension checks) assess lower eyelid horizontal laxity; **distraction** (forward pull distance) over **6** to **8** mm or delayed **snap-back** (slow recoil) mandates lateral **canthopexy** (tendon tightening) or **canthoplasty** (tendon reconstruction) to prevent post-blepharoplasty **ectropion** (outward lid roll with scleral show).

steps.say: Ptosis numbers are separating tendon failure from muscle failure. Margin reflex distance one of four to four and a half millimetres is measuring lid height, and levator excursion of twelve to fifteen millimetres is measuring power. Low height with good power is meaning aponeurosis repair.
steps.tx: **Blepharoptosis** (drooping upper lid) is assessed by margin reflex distance-1 **MRD1** (corneal light reflex to lid margin) normal **4.0** to **4.5** mm and **levator excursion** (lid travel from downgaze to upgaze) normal **12** to **15** mm. Low MRD1 with preserved excursion means dehisced aponeurosis; poor excursion means weak muscle needing a sling.

steps.say: Pressure behind the eye is blinding within hours and is being released at the bedside. Retrobulbar bleeding is raising intraocular pressure into a compartment syndrome. Immediate lateral canthotomy with inferior cantholysis is cutting the corner and the lower retractors.
steps.tx: **Retrobulbar haematoma** (bleeding behind the globe) is an ophthalmic emergency causing acute **intraocular hypertension** (eye pressure spike) and compartment syndrome, requiring immediate bedside **lateral canthotomy** (cutting the outer lid corner) and **inferior cantholysis** (releasing the lower lid retractors). No scan, no delay: cut first at the bedside.

vis.alt: Skull with fracture lines plus an orbital panel showing blowout CT and the lateral canthotomy release.
vis.caption: The canthotomy panel: lateral canthotomy with inferior cantholysis releases retrobulbar pressure. Credit: StewardMD.
